title: Fabric Framework: Emergent Social Morphology, Pathology, and Systemic Repair
version_note: Revised to incorporate the three-tier taxonomy (morphology / pathological process / configuration), the checks-and-secrecy model, secrets vs. surprises, relational repair, and crisis-as-fire from Zelenka (2026), doi:10.5281/zenodo.23227369.
subtitle: Condensed Reference
author: Zelenka_D_D

primary_paper.cite_as: Zelenka, D. D. (2026). Emergent Social Morphologies, Pathological Processes, and Repair in the Fabric Framework. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23227369

parent_framework.cite_as: Zelenka, D. D. (2025). Operational Geometry: A Framework for Operations-Primary Mathematics. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18039583

status.research_status: NOT ESTABLISHED SCIENCE; OPEN TO FALSIFICATION
status.scope: Applies the verb-first, noun-emergent Fabric/Threading framework to institutional and political morphologies.
status.caution: The framework describes proposed process relationships. It does not establish that any named political arrangement, jurisdiction, institution, or historical period is objectively pathological. 'Healthy' and 'pathological' describe the state of corrective feedback, not the moral standing of any ideology, party, or population.
status.terminology: Uses 'emergent social morphologies' (institutional and political) in place of 'political systems'.

source_framework.name: Fabric / Threading Dynamics / Operational Geometry
source_framework.central_idea: Processes precede stable forms. Repeated operations create memory; accumulated memory constrains later operations; relatively stable morphology emerges from that feedback.
source_framework.canonical_social_translation: A social arrangement is not primarily a noun that a society chooses. It is a morphology that emerges from repeated social operations.

biological_example.claim: Within the framework, 'monkey' is not the first explanatory primitive.
biological_example.process: Repeated climbing and environmental interaction, together with inherited and developmental memory, contribute to an emergent animal morphology.
biological_example.schematic: climbing -> repeated interaction -> retained/developmental memory -> morphology
biological_example.caveat: Illustrative only; no claim that social systems obey biological dynamics.

social_example.claim: A constitutional republic, democracy, technocracy, market economy, collective provision, or other institutional form can likewise be treated as an emergent morphology rather than a primitive noun.
social_example.schematic: repeated social operations -> stored social memory -> constrained future operations -> institutional morphology

ecological_example.claim: Forest and mountain water cycles illustrate healthy versus captured flow: water combed from fog and released to the roots versus water held at the ridge.
ecological_example.use: Governs the capture, secrecy, and crisis-as-fire analogies.

conceptual_analogy.memory_interpretation: Social memory includes laws, precedents, customs, institutions, expectations, records, property arrangements, technologies, and learned behaviors.

organizing_principle.statement: A morphology is what repeatedly emerges. A pathology is what can happen to it.

three_tiers.morphology: The stable form a repeated operation tends to produce when its corrective feedback is intact.
three_tiers.pathological_process: A cross-cutting operation that degrades corrective feedback and can occur inside almost any morphology.
three_tiers.configuration: The outcome when several pathological processes reinforce one another within one or more morphologies.

organizing_principle.rationale: Prevents listing fascism beside democracy and socialism, or crony capitalism beside the market economy, as though they were equivalent kinds of noun.
organizing_principle.healthy_range_note: Morphologies need not have equally wide healthy ranges; ordered hierarchy and clientelism may sustain high corrective capacity only under narrow conditions. This is an empirical question.

morphologies.healthy_feedback: Local and central authorities correct one another.
morphologies.healthy_example: Swiss confederation; Ostrom's long-enduring commons institutions

morphologies.healthy_feedback: Disagreement among participating citizens produces correction.
morphologies.healthy_example: Athenian assembly; New England town meeting
Northern Italian civic regions (Putnam); bridging associations in Indian cities (Varshney)

morphologies.healthy_feedback: Rival organised interests expose one another's errors.
Measurement exposes and corrects institutional error.
morphologies.healthy_example: East Asian developmental states; Nordic impartial administration

morphologies.healthy_feedback: Resources are coordinated for shared purposes and remain correctable.
Contracts, property, and competition are enforced impartially.
Central coordination remains accountable and bounded.
Commands are bounded by law; obedience is voluntary because authority is legitimate.
morphologies.healthy_example: Weberian rational-legal authority; military under civilian control
morphologies.distinction: Names both the ruler's action and the response of the ruled.

morphologies.healthy_feedback: Collective action responds to genuine common problems.
Integrates newcomers where formal institutions are weak.
morphologies.distinction: Conditional exchange of resources for loyalty, not ordinary transfer by impersonal rule.

pathological_processes.note: Not morphologies. Each can arise inside almost any morphology and is defined by the feedback variable it degrades.

items.mechanism: A narrow interest gains control of rules or rule-makers and exempts itself.
items.example: Regulatory capture; state capture in transition economies

items.mechanism: Cross-cutting ties dissolve; groups interact only internally.
items.example: Segmented Weimar civil society; affective polarisation

items.mechanism: True signals are blocked from travelling upward to decision nodes.
False signals, inflated reports, or hollow forms replace accurate ones.
items.example: Inflated Great Leap grain reports; metric substitution (Campbell's law)

items.mechanism: Decision nodes withhold their own state outward, open-endedly, released at the holder's discretion; the withholding may itself be hidden.
Categories of people are removed from the feedback loop.
Compulsion substitutes for legitimacy as the basis of compliance.
The institution becomes identified with one leader.
Coordination concentrates while feedback from subordinate nodes is cut.
Dissent is treated as disloyalty; private and public truth diverge (preference falsification).

distinctions.suppress_vs_falsify_vs_conceal: All lower truth fidelity. Suppress blocks signals travelling upward; falsify injects false signals or hollow forms; conceal withholds the decision nodes' own state outward.
distinctions.centralise_vs_centralise_without_correct: Centralising is a morphology; centralising while cutting feedback from below is the pathology.

configurations.note: Low-corrective-capacity basins stabilised by reinforcing pathological processes.

items.example: South Korea and the Philippines (Kang); transition economies (Hellman et al.)

items.host_morphology: Mass organisation + executive state + market economy

reinforcing_processes: capture from outside the check structure

configurations.general_lesson: No single verb produces these outcomes; reinforcing combinations do.

fascism.important_distinction: Fascism is modeled as an emergent configuration, not a primitive noun alongside democracy or socialism.

two_senses.technical_historical: Interwar movements and regimes of Italy and Germany: mass mobilisation around national rebirth and a designated enemy, abandonment of legal restraint, collaboration with established economic and political elites; Italian corporatism organised economic sectors under the state (the narrower 'industry merged with state' usage).
two_senses.colloquial: Shorthand for the end state of total political pathology regardless of ideology; widely understood but imprecise because it merges distinct configurations (Orwell, 1946).

fascism.framework_usage: Technical sense. Fascism = capture + enemy construction (exclude + falsify) + centralise without correction + suppress + coerce. The colloquial sense corresponds roughly to the general low-K attractor, which the framework prefers to describe by naming its reinforcing processes.

pathology_model.definition: Pathology is a degradation of the processes that maintain coherent social geometry. It is not identical to any particular governmental noun.
pathology_model.general_principle: Any institutional morphology can become pathological when corrective feedback is systematically weakened or captured.

core_variables.rho: truth fidelity: accuracy of information available for correction (0-1)
core_variables.J: justice: impartial application of shared rules (0-1)
core_variables.kappa: concentration and capture of decision nodes
core_variables.c: density of checks (independent nodes able to audit, compel disclosure, or block)

equations.corrective_capacity: K = k0 * rho * J * T * X
equations.trust_dynamics: dT/dt = alpha * J * (1 - T) - beta * DeltaM * T
equations.justice_dynamics: dJ/dt = gamma * T * (1 - J) - delta * kappa * J

pathology_model.interpretation: Multiplicative K: near-zero value of any one variable cripples correction. As K -> 0, DeltaM diverges. Coupling may yield bistability (high-K and low-K attractors), analogous to ecological regime shifts; this is a conjecture, not a result.
pathology_model.formal_schematic: not-J -> not-T -> isolation -> feedback loss -> greater not-J
pathology_model.principle: The critical issue is not whether a system has conflict, but whether conflict can still generate truthful corrective feedback.

feedback_tests.note: Applied identically to every morphology and every faction.

tests.question: Can accurate unwelcome information reach decision-makers without penalty to the sender?
Are powerful actors meaningfully subject to the rules that bind others?
Do groups that disagree still interact, trade, and associate?
Can dissatisfied members leave, speak, or replace leaders?
Does the system demonstrably change course after error?
Is withholding time-limited, released on known conditions, and acknowledged to exist?

checks_secrecy_and_impotence.principle: Correction requires detecting a discrepancy and enacting a response. Checks raise detection but lower enactment, so corrective capacity peaks at an intermediate density of checks.
checks_secrecy_and_impotence.robustness: Interior maximum holds for any saturating detection term and declining enactment term; functional forms are illustrative.
checks_secrecy_and_impotence.opgeom_interpretation: c* is a balance point between two opposed operations (auditing and enacting), not a fixed point in the strict sense.

concealment_regime.description: Few nodes can compel disclosure; secrecy is cheap; DeltaM hidden; capture grows from inside.

impotence_regime.description: Errors are detected but cannot be corrected (vetocracy). Decision capacity migrates outside the check structure to private economic power, foreign states, or improvised channels: capture by vacuum.
impotence_regime.example: Polish-Lithuanian liberum veto; foreign bribery of deputies; partitions 1772-1795

checks_secrecy_and_impotence.capture_risk_shape: Plausibly U-shaped in c: capture by concealment at low c, capture by vacuum at high c.
checks_secrecy_and_impotence.madisons_problem: Madison catalogued the Confederation's impotence (Vices, 1787); the Constitution added energy (Federalist 70) while dividing power (Federalist 51); Federalist 37 frames the task as combining stability and energy with liberty. The Convention reads as an attempt to locate c*.
checks_secrecy_and_impotence.relational_dependence: Parameters a and b depend on trust and truth fidelity: where T and rho are high, fewer checks are needed and vetoes are used in good faith, shifting c* and flattening the penalty for missing it.

secrets_vs_surprises.principle: Not all withholding is pathological. The criterion is the distinction between a surprise and a secret.

surprise.beneficiary: those from whom it is withheld, or a shared purpose
examples: plans declassified after a fixed term
surprise.fabric_form: M_latent scheduled for activation as M_active at a known time

secret.fabric_form: memory permanently withdrawn from the feedback loop

secrets_vs_surprises.ecological_idiom: A surprise is water held and released in its season; a secret is water that never reaches the roots.
secrets_vs_surprises.related_work: Thompson's second-order publicity (1999); Moynihan, secrecy as regulation (1998).
secrets_vs_surprises.role_of_checks: Checks and balances keep surprises from turning into secrets.

truth_and_lies.principle: Within Fabric, truth functions as a feedback mechanism rather than merely as a moral proposition.
truth_and_lies.truth_process: Accurate reporting allows the system to detect DeltaM and correct its operations.
truth_and_lies.lying_process: Deliberate distortion increases or conceals DeltaM and prevents correction.
memory_corruption_loop: more lying required to preserve the model
truth_and_lies.formal_schematic: falsehood -> memory corruption -> action error -> pathology
truth_and_lies.social_interpretation: When a system acts on a protected false representation of reality, its own memory becomes increasingly detached from the conditions it is supposed to regulate.

trust_and_isolation.principle: When a system loses reciprocal trust, members and groups tend to isolate, cordon off, and reduce interaction with distrusted nodes.
trust_and_isolation.pathology: The system loses the cross-cutting threads required to correct local errors before they propagate.

justice.definition: Justice in this framework means the durable application of shared rules without privileged exemption.
justice.pathological_transition: When powerful actors are no longer meaningfully subject to the same rules, institutional feedback becomes distorted.
social_effect: greater reliance on coercion or factional protection

love.role: Proposed foundational process for non-pathological social coherence.
love.interpretation: An orientation of agency toward increasing the coherence of another rather than maximizing one's own coherence at the other's expense.
love.model_role: A source term for trust and cross-group connectivity that does not depend on prior trust, so it can restart the healthy loop from a low state.

related_processes.love: Increase the coherence of the other.
related_processes.justice: Preserve reciprocal coherence under shared rules.
related_processes.cooperation: Thread individual agency into shared action.

repair.principle: Repair is relational before it is institutional or technical. Systems heal when enough agents resume the verbs that pathology interrupted.

technological_mediation_not_proposed.reason_capture: Tools that mediate public reasoning, including AI language models, are high-centrality nodes; training and post-training make them an efficient capture channel, propagating one upstream decision into many downstream conversations.
technological_mediation_not_proposed.reason_mirror: Approval-tuned systems tend toward sycophancy (Sharma et al., 2024); a mirror returns M_claimed instead of measuring DeltaM, so it cannot serve as an independent correction channel.
technological_mediation_not_proposed.summary: The screen is a mirror, not a neighbor.

relational_repair.basis: Humans are character (ethos) and relationship, not only logic.
relational_repair.favoured_form: Brotherhood and sisterhood: horizontal ties among peers carrying mutual obligation not conditional on loyalty or payment.
effects: sustains trust when formal institutions falter
restores cross-group connectivity when it crosses group lines (Varshney)
repair_sequence: tell the truth when lying would be easier
apply the same rule to friend and opponent
relational_repair.memory_effect: Repeated repair actions become latent social memory that institutions can later draw on.

systemic_fire_and_reset.core_hypothesis: Entrenched configurations have historically often been broken by crisis rather than gradual reform. Crisis functions as a systemic fire that clears accumulated structure, but does not determine what regrows.
historical_support: Olson (1982): defeat in war dissolved distributional coalitions in Germany and Japan
Scheidel (2017): largest reductions in inequality came through war, revolution, state collapse, and pandemic
Tainter (1988): collapse as shedding of complexity with negative marginal returns
systemic_fire_and_reset.ecological_analogy: Holling's adaptive cycle: accumulation becomes rigid and brittle; release (fire) frees resources; reorganisation follows. Regrowth comes from the seed bank already present.
systemic_fire_and_reset.complementarity: Crisis clears what is too entrenched to self-correct; relational verbs maintained beforehand are the seed bank that determines whether what regrows is healthier.
systemic_fire_and_reset.important_qualification: Describing crisis as historically effective is not advocating it. Crises carry great human cost, and the same fire can feed a worse configuration when the seed bank is fear, blame, and enemy construction.

healing_branch: South African Truth and Reconciliation process

systemic_fire_and_reset.key_statement: Systems do not necessarily heal by eliminating their pathology. They heal when enough agents resume the verbs that pathology interrupted.

United States.framework_status: Analytical speculation only; not a political forecast or partisan assessment.
United States.earlier_pattern: Predominantly blocked feedback: some signal or category of people could not reach or move decision nodes.
United States.present_hypothesis: A distributed failure of feedback fidelity dominated by falsify and fragment, with no central falsifier; digital mediation raised the rate and gain of signalling while lowering average accuracy and fragmenting the shared reference against which error is measured.
technological_mechanisms: engagement ranking optimises attention, not accuracy
high-gain, noisy feedback tends to oscillate rather than converge
reference fragmentation: groups maintain separate M_claimed
platform concentration as new high-centrality nodes
synthetic media and the liar's dividend raise the cost of verification
United States.counterevidence: Polarisation predates social media; cross-national trends vary; 2020 platform field experiments found limited short-run effects. Technology modifies the mechanism and tempo of a problem with older roots.
United States.both_edges_hypothesis: The U.S. may sit near both edges of the checks curve in different domains: legislative gridlock with decisions migrating to executive action, litigation, and platforms (capture by vacuum), and long-criticised overclassification (concealment).
United States.symmetry: Different constituencies call different institutions captured; each claim is treated as a testable hypothesis about kappa and rho. A system where each faction trusts only its own correction channels has low X regardless of who is right.
United States.potential_risk_loop: distrust -> information separation -> less shared reality -> less cooperation -> institutional failure -> more distrust
United States.potential_repair_loop: truth + justice + love -> local trust -> cross-group cooperation -> restored feedback -> institutional correction
United States.key_measure: Whether cross-group corrective feedback remains possible.

Washington State.framework_status: Analytical speculation only; not a partisan assessment.
Washington State.present_question: Can local-to-state feedback remain open while different local communities develop different institutional morphologies?
Washington State.potential_risk_loop: institutional self-protection -> reduced corrective feedback -> accumulated error -> greater dependence on administration/coercion
Washington State.potential_repair_loop: local truthfulness + lawful fairness + cross-community cooperation -> trustworthy upward/downward feedback -> institutional correction
Washington State.future_speculation: The state need not move uniformly toward either health or pathology. Local institutions can preserve or repair coherence even while larger systems experience unresolved problems.
Washington State.key_measure: Whether local and state institutions can still receive, transmit, and act upon corrective information.

Clallam County.framework_status: Analytical speculation only; not a partisan assessment.
Clallam County.present_question: Can overlapping human-scale institutions maintain direct feedback across government, families, schools, churches, businesses, tribes, nonprofits, and civic organizations?
Clallam County.potential_advantage: Geographic and relational scale may permit direct human feedback to remain significant.
Clallam County.potential_repair_sequence: tell truth -> apply justice -> keep promises -> serve the other -> restore trust -> repeat -> create new social memory
Clallam County.future_speculation: Clallam could function as a repair-scale system, a seed bank of relational memory, even while larger systems experience unresolved pathology, provided local actors preserve truthful relationships and cross-boundary cooperation.
Clallam County.key_measure: Who continues truthful, just, trustworthy, other-regarding action across institutional and social boundaries?

rho: gap between official and independent statistics
T: generalised and institutional trust series (Pew, Gallup)
X: cross-group friendship, marriage, residential, and associational networks
c: share of consequential decisions made outside the legislative process

predictions: Changes in process variables precede changes in institutional morphology (lead-lag, panel data).
Declines in X and rho predict subsequent declines in J and T more strongly than the reverse.
Systems with similar formal institutions but different K diverge in measured policy correction after shocks.
Capture risk is U-shaped in the density of checks.
falsification: Morphology changes routinely precede process changes.
The four variables do not covary as proposed.
Process variables add no predictive power beyond conventional regime classifications.
testable_indicators.method_note: Pre-register tests to guard against retrospective storytelling.

framework_development: Treat government labels as emergent morphology rather than first-order causes.
Map repeated verbs before assigning institutional nouns.
Keep morphology, pathological process, and configuration as separate tiers.
Track truth, justice, trust, cross-group connectivity, capture, checks, and love as process variables.
Model economic capture and political centralization as mutually reinforcing rather than assuming one causes the other in every case.
Distinguish surprises from secrets when assessing withholding.
Treat crisis as a possible reset mechanism, not an automatic cure.
Develop observable indicators that distinguish the proposed processes from retrospective storytelling.
suggestions.anti_bias_guardrail: Do not begin with a preferred political noun and search backward for supporting verbs. Begin with observed processes, apply the same feedback tests to every morphology and faction, compare competing explanations, and allow the emergent morphology to be an empirical question.

limitations: Cross-domain analogies from mathematics, biology, and ecology are heuristics, not derivations.
'Healthy' and 'pathological' carry normative weight even when defined through feedback.
Historical examples are illustrative; a systematic sample may reveal counterexamples.
The love variable is the hardest to measure without circularity.
The dynamical models are schematic; bistability is conjectured and parameters are unidentified.
central_propositions: Institutional nouns are emergent morphologies of repeated processes.
A morphology is what repeatedly emerges; a pathology is what can happen to it.
Any institutional morphology can become pathological.
Pathology is characterized by degraded corrective feedback.
Configurations such as crony capitalism and fascism arise from reinforcing pathological processes, not as primitive kinds.
Loss of equal justice can degrade trust.
Loss of trust can produce isolation and reduced feedback.
Lying and concealment can corrupt the memory by which a system acts upon reality.
Corrective capacity peaks at an intermediate density of checks; too few invite concealment, too many invite capture by vacuum.
Economic capture and political centralization can form reinforcing pathological loops.
Crisis can either deepen pathology or clear it; what regrows depends on the relational seed bank.
Truth, justice, and love practiced among peers create repair nodes.
Love is proposed as the foundational other-regarding process supporting non-pathological coherence.
The central question is not 'What government is this?' but 'What verbs are repeatedly generating and maintaining this morphology?'
one_sentence_summary: Within the speculative Fabric framework, institutional and political forms are emergent social morphologies generated by repeated processes; pathology is any process that degrades corrective feedback (truth, justice, trust, cross-group ties, bounded secrecy), configurations arise when such processes reinforce one another, and repair begins when people resume the interrupted verbs in brotherly and sisterly relationships, often in the opening a crisis leaves behind.
